author: Gowon Akpodonor
title: Onwuzurike qualifies for 200m semifinals, Ogazi, Udo seek final tickets today
text:
United States-based speed star, Udodi Onwuzurike , yesterday, produced an impressive performance to qualify for the men’s 200m semifinals at the ongoing Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games . He won his first-round heat in 20.31 seconds.
All eyes will be on the duo of Samuel Ogazi and Edidiong Udo today, as Team Nigeria continue its quest for more medals at the Games.
Running on Lane Five in Heat Five, Onwuzurike crossed the finish line first with the second-fastest qualifying time overall, behind only Jamaica’s Jevaughn Powell, who clocked 20.28 seconds.
Ghana’s Joseph Paul Amoah and Jamaica’s Christopher Taylor followed with identical 20.36-second performances, while Kenya’s Zablon Ekwam ran a season’s best 20.42 seconds and England’s Zharnel Hughes qualified in 20.45 seconds.
The top 16 performers from the opening round progressed to the semifinals, with Onwuzurike emerging as one of the leading contenders after his commanding heat victory.
He will now be aiming to carry that momentum into the next round as he continues his quest for a Commonwealth Games medal in Glasgow.
His female counterparts, Obi Jennifer Chukwuka and Olayinka Olajide, will, however, face stern opposition as they bid for places in the women’s 200m final this evening.
Chukwuka, who owns a personal and season’s best of 23.26 seconds, has been drawn in the opening semifinal alongside Jamaica’s Alana Reid, England’s Success Eduan, Australia’s Torrie Lewis, Canada’s Frederique Chiasson, the British Virgin Islands’ Beyonce Defreitas, Malawi’s Asimenye Simwaka and Kenya’s Milcent Ndoro.
Reid, with a season’s best of 22.29 seconds, starts as the favourite in the race.
Olajide, whose personal and season’s best stands at 23.14 seconds, has an equally demanding assignment in the second semifinal.
She will line up against the British Virgin Islands’ world-class sprinter Adaejah Hodge, who boasts the fastest entry time of 21.68 seconds, Jamaica’s Ashanti Moore, Australia’s Monique Hanlon, Canada’s Marie-Eloise Leclair, Scotland’s Alyson Bell, Tanzania’s Winfrida Makenji and Singapore’s Veronica Shanti Pereira.
Only the first two finishers in each semifinal, along with the next two fastest athletes overall, will progress to the final.
Both Nigerians will therefore need either automatic qualification or one of the two fastest non-automatic qualifying times to keep their medal hopes alive.
Meanwhile, the duo of Ogazi and Udo will target a place in the 400m final today.
Ogazi has won both the NCAA Indoor Championships and NCAA Outdoor Championships titles in the 400m event this season, setting an African record in the former and an NCAA record in the latter.
Udo, who won his 400m heat on Tuesday, told The Guardian yesterday that “my target is to get to the final on Thursday. From there, anything can happen. It will be a major achievement being my first appearance for Nigeria to win a medal of any colour,” Udo said.
While Ogazi is in the first heat today, Udo will compete in the last heat of the 400m.
